newsitem.title: USA: CalPERS health care rates to rise 2.7 pct in 1998.
newsitem.headline: CalPERS health care rates to rise 2.7 pct in 1998.

text.p: The California Public Employees' Retirement System (CalPERS) said on Tuesday that health insurance premiums for the bulk of its one million members would increase by less than three percent next year.
The CalPERS Health Benefits Committee approved rate increases for its 11 participating health maintenance organizations (HMOs) averaging 2.7 percent for 1998.
The CalPERS committee also approved a first-ever three-year contract with PacifiCare of California, the HMO subsidiary of PacifiCare Health Systems Inc, to assure stable rates.

PacifiCare will receive a 2.5 percent rate increase for the calendar year beginning January 1, 1998 as part of the new proposed agreement. The rates for 1999 and 2000 would be based on increases tied to the Consumer Price Index.
The other 10 participating HMOs signed one-year contracts.
The rates and HMO contracts are expected to receive final approval Wednesday by the CalPERS Board of Administration.

The new CalPERS rates are far below industry expectations of up to a 10 percent increase as well as below the latest Consumer Price Index of 2.9 percent for medical cost inflation during the past year, CalPERS said.

"The contracts approved today very effectively balance our requirements for quality health care, affordable cost and improved customer service," said Kurato Shimada, chair of the CalPERS Health Benefits Committee.
CalPERS said the 1998 rates will take into account soaring drug prices for the various CalPERS health plans -- drug prices that have increased by an average of 13 percent.
The new rates will go into effect January 1, 1998, for CalPERS health plan members -- 76 percent of whom are enrolled in HMOs, CalPERS said.

CalPERS is the second largest purchaser of health care in the United States, exceeded in size only by the federal government. CalPERS membership includes one million public employees and their families.
